records.title: An Allogeneic PBMC-Organoid Co-culture Platform for Evaluating Immunotherapy Efficacy and T-Cell-Mediated Antitumor Immunity.
records.abstract: Traditional 2D cell lines and mouse xenograft models have limitations in recapitulating the complexity of the tumor microenvironment (TME) and dynamic interactions between tumor and immune cells, creating an urgent need for models to evaluate immunotherapies. Patient-derived organoids (PDOs), which retain key features of original tumors, offer a platform for dissecting the TME when co-cultured with peripheral blood mononuclear cells (PBMCs). However, challenges such as inter-batch variability of PBMCs and difficulties in autologous PBMC acquisition hinder their clinical translation. This study established four stably passaged colorectal cancer organoid models and developed an allogeneic PBMC-organoid co-culture platform to investigate the immune activation and cytotoxic potential of allogeneic PBMCs. Results showed that vacuolated-structured organoids are associated with the increased proportion of CD8+ T cells in PBMCs within the co-culture system. PBMCs exhibited stronger cytotoxicity against microsatellite-stable (MSS) organoids with low PD-L1 expression, while the anti-PD-1 antibody Keytruda significantly enhanced their antitumor effects on high PD-L1-expressing organoids. The allogeneic co-culture model developed here overcomes the limitations of autologous PBMC acquisition, providing an efficient and versatile proof-of-concept platform for pre-clinical screening of immunotherapeutic drugs. Distinct from prior allogeneic co-culture systems that rely on healthy donor immune cells, our platform uniquely integrates patient-derived allogeneic PBMCs with tumor organoids, providing preliminary proof-of-concept evidence that tumor-intrinsic features may influence immunotherapy responses based on tumor-intrinsic features while preserving the pathological relevance of cancer patient immune profiles.

records.title: A patient-derived bladder cancer organoid and xenograft platform for personalized drug response prediction and salvage therapeutics screening.
records.abstract: Therapeutic resistance remains a major challenge in bladder cancer treatment. The aim of this study was to develop and validate a bladder cancer patient-derived organoid (PDO)-based platform for treatment response prediction and individualized salvage therapy screening. A total of 101 patients with bladder cancer were enrolled to establish 75 PDO lines. The optimal culture medium was determined by transcriptome analysis. Consistency validation was performed via histopathology, immunohistochemistry, whole-exome sequencing, and transcriptomic profiling. A three-step high-throughput screening pipeline for 288 approved agents was developed to identify salvage therapies for patients who were multidrug-resistant, which was validated in patient-derived xenograft (PDX) models. A suspension coculture system was constructed to evaluate HER2-targeted chimeric antigen receptor T (CAR-T) cell cytotoxicity and activation. FGF4 supplementation significantly enhanced the 3D growth and establishment efficiency of PDOs, yielding a biobank of 75 bladder cancer PDOs. These PDOs faithfully recapitulated the multidimensional features of parental tumors, and showed preliminary concordance with observed clinical treatment responses (cisplatin, gemcitabine, and epirubicin). To address drug resistance, the high-throughput drug screening pipeline maps individualized sensitivity profiles in four cases. In a patient who was multidrug-resistant, idarubicin was pinpointed as a potent candidate agent, with efficacy confirmed in PDX models. To extend the screening platform beyond chemotherapeutics and cover cellular immunotherapies, we verified that the coculture system enabled HER2 expression-dependent CAR-T cytotoxicity evaluation. This integrated bladder cancer PDO platform provides a clinically relevant individualized tool for treatment response prediction and individualized salvage therapy selection, particularly for patients with multidrug-resistant disease. Its application may support tailored therapeutic decision-making across chemotherapy, targeted therapy, and cellular immunotherapy.

records.title: Engineered organoid platforms for mechanistic studies of gut microbiota-cancer interactions.
records.abstract: Associations between the gut microbiota and cancer are increasingly reproducible at the cohort level, but association alone cannot establish whether a microorganism, microbial product, or metabolite directly alters tumor-relevant host biology. Engineered organoid systems address this gap by placing defined microbial exposures against human or genetically specified epithelia under experimentally controlled conditions. The strength of the resulting inference depends on platform architecture. Three-dimensional organoids preserve epithelial organization but restrict luminal access; microinjection and apical-out configurations enable direct microbial exposure; organoid-derived monolayers permit directional sampling and barrier measurements; and microfluidic systems add flow, oxygen gradients, and longer-term host-microbe co-culture. Tumor organoids and defined immune or stromal co-cultures can be added when the biological question requires cancer-specific or multicellular readouts. This review evaluates these platforms according to the mechanistic questions they can answer and distinguishes evidence from live microorganisms, complex communities, cell-free microbial products, purified metabolites, and clinical associations. The strongest organoid-based evidence currently concerns microbial genotoxicity, epithelial transformation, barrier and repair responses, selected tumor-growth phenotypes, and intestinal treatment toxicity. Direct organoid evidence linking the gut microbiota to distant, non-gastrointestinal tumors remains limited despite substantial clinical and animal data. We further discuss how physicochemical control, omics-based benchmarking, and standardized reporting can improve reproducibility without adding unnecessary model complexity. The central requirement is explicit matching of experimental architecture to the causal claim being tested.

records.title: Autophagy Modulation Influenced the Spermatogenesis in Rodent Testicular Organoids and Diabetic Condition.
records.abstract: Here, the effect of autophagy activity was investigated in rat testicular organoids embedded in alginate/gelatin (Alg/Gel) hydrogel. Additionally, we monitored the spermatogenesis potential in diabetic mice following the administration of metformin (Met) and/or hydroxychloroquine (HCQ). Alg/Gel hydrogel was fabricated, and its physicochemical properties were studied. The survival rate of freshly isolated rat whole testicular tissue cells being plated on the Alg/Gel hydrogel surface was monitored after 7 days. Rat testicular organoids were embedded in Alg/Gel hydrogel and exposed to 15 µM HCQ and/or 5 µM Met for 7 days. Histological examination was conducted to assess OCT3/4+ progenitors and maturing sperm cells. Using western blotting, the levels of autophagic markers Beclin-1, LC3, and P62 were evaluated. Diabetic mice received 120 mg/kg body weight Met and/or 70 mg/kg bodyweight HCQ for 4 weeks, followed by histological examinations and sperm analysis. The fabricated Alg/Gel hydrogel demonstrated suitable physicochemical properties, which correlated with an increased survival rate of whole testicular tissue cells compared to the control group (P<0.05). Data indicated a promotion of autophagy (Beclin-1↑, LC3-II/-I ratio↑, P62↓) and an inhibition of autophagy (LC3↓) in testicular organoids after treatment with Met and HCQ, respectively, compared to the control group (P<0.05). These changes were accompanied by an induction of SOD activity in Met-treated testicular organoids (P<0.05). In the presence of Met and HCQ, OCT3/4+ progenitors were reduced in rat organoids compared to non-treated control organoids (P<0.05). Administration of Met, but not HCQ, in diabetic mice was able to restore some sperm parameters, such as motility, and reduce abnormal morphologies compared to the matched diabetic mice (P<0.05). Regulation of autophagy can influence spermatogenesis capacity, affecting seminiferous tubule progenitors, maturation, and sperm parameters. In studies of rat testicular organoids and diabetic mice, these findings suggest that the autophagy response is a promising signaling pathway target in subfertile or infertile males.

records.title: Subtype or state? Rethinking the apCAF paradox and fibroblast plasticity in gastrointestinal cancers.
records.abstract: Antigen-presenting cancer-associated fibroblasts (apCAFs), commonly defined by MHC class II molecules, CD74, and related transcriptional programs, exhibit divergent functions across gastrointestinal tumors. In pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma, mesothelium-derived apCAFs promote regulatory T-cell differentiation and suppress effector responses, whereas their abundance in gastric cancer is associated with earlier-stage disease, longer survival, and improved immunotherapy responses. This paradox may reflect microenvironmental context and classifications that conflate transcriptional state, cellular origin, and immune function. apCAFs may therefore represent reversible, context-dependent states defined by origin, MHC class II-restricted antigen presentation, and co-stimulatory capacity. We propose a two-layer model that has not been validated in apCAFs. In this model, the chromatin accessibility of CIITA, CD40, CD80, and CD86 constructs a functional licensing range, while interferon - γ (IFN - γ), interleukin-1 (IL-1), and transforming growth factor - β (TGF - β) guide the formation of specific phenotypes within this range. Insufficient co-stimulation may favor immune tolerance; activation of co-stimulatory programs may support CD4+ T-cell help and CD8+ T-cell infiltration. Treatment-induced changes in CAF composition may reflect selective survival or genuine state transitions. Distinguishing these mechanisms requires lineage tracing, longitudinal single-cell transcriptomic and chromatin profiling, and patient-derived organoid-fibroblast co-cultures. Neoadjuvant therapy and serial endoscopic sampling provide feasible settings for capturing transient states. This framework supports replacing broad CAF depletion with temporally and state-informed functional reprogramming.

records.title: Development-Informed Microsphere Assemblies Enable Spatiotemporally Programmed Bone-Vascular Organoid-Like Constructs for Large Bone Defect Repair.
records.abstract: Large segmental bone defects are difficult to repair because endogenous stem-cell activation, vascular ingrowth, and osteogenic maturation are insufficient to rebuild organized bone tissue. Bone organoids offer a promising regenerative strategy, but current systems are limited by Matrigel dependence, poor vascularization, low post-implantation survival, and inadequate reconstruction of hierarchical bone microarchitecture. Here, we report a development-informed, Matrigel-free bone-vascular organoid-like platform that integrates single-cell-guided gene programming with an osteoinductive and vascular-permissive microsphere matrix. Single-cell analysis identified BMP4 and VEGFA as key genes linking osteogenic commitment with vascular morphogenesis. Engineered BMSCs were used to sequentially generate osteoinductive bone organoid-like constructs(OLCs) and bone-vascular OLCs with coordinated osteogenic and angiogenic activity. Microfluidic GelMA/PEO/bioactive glass(BG) microsphere clusters provided adhesive, mineralization-promoting, and space-making cues for cell migration, matrix deposition, and endothelial invasion. Within seven days, the OLCs developed mineralized matrix, vascular-like sprouting, and early vascular-like microchannels. After implantation into rabbit femoral defects, they enhanced vascularized bone formation, defect bridging, and trabecular remodeling. This work demonstrates the power of development-informed, Matrigel-free bone-vascular OLCs in accelerating vascularized bone regeneration for large segmental bone defect repair.

records.title: Single-cell perturbation prediction near experimental reproducibility with GENESIS.
records.abstract: Single-cell perturbation atlases now measure cellular responses across millions of cells, but the number of possible combinations of biological contexts, perturbations, doses and other experimental variables make exhaustive measurements infeasible. Here, we present GENESIS (Generative ENErgy-based Single-cell Intervention Simulator), a generative framework that predicts single-cell response distributions directly from the covariates defining an experimental condition. GENESIS uses a lightweight neural network trained with the energy score, a strictly proper scoring rule for distributions. We introduce an experiment-calibrated evaluation framework in which prediction error is interpreted relative to the reproducibility of repeated measurements of the same condition. Across the Tahoe-100M small-molecule atlas and a large PBMC cytokine atlas, GENESIS significantly outperforms existing generative models and statistical baselines and approaches experimental reproducibility on independently repeated conditions. Importantly, GENESIS remains accurate when trained on only a fraction of the available experimental conditions or cells, and generated profiles recover experimentally observed context-dependent transcriptional programs. At comparable training-cell budgets, GENESIS achieves more accurate predictions when measurements span more experimental conditions rather than profiling fewer conditions more deeply. Together, these findings suggest a complementary strategy for perturbation studies: broader, lower-depth measurements can expand experimental coverage, while GENESIS augments sparsely sampled populations and predicts responses in unmeasured conditions.

records.title: MultiFlow: coupled flow matching for predicting single-cell multiomic perturbation responses in unseen cellular contexts.
records.abstract: Predicting cellular responses to perturbation requires resolving coordinated changes across molecular layers, yet most single-cell perturbation models focus on transcriptional responses alone. Here we present MultiFlow, a coupled flow-matching framework that unifies generation and perturbation prediction of paired gene expression and chromatin accessibility. Through bidirectional information exchange between RNA and ATAC generative flows, MultiFlow learns how their joint distribution depends on cellular context and perturbation identity. Across multiomic generation benchmarks, MultiFlow accurately reproduced paired RNA-ATAC states and their population distributions. In multiome perturbation benchmarks, MultiFlow achieved the strongest overall performance in predicting both gene-expression and chromatin-accessibility perturbation responses, outperforming modality-specific perturbation-prediction methods in cell types whose perturbed states were withheld from training. Joint multiomic modeling further preserved perturbation-induced coordination between modalities, including concordant peak-gene effects and cross-modal cellular neighborhood structure. These results establish MultiFlow as a unified generative framework for modeling paired molecular states and predicting their coordinated perturbation responses across cellular contexts. Code and tutorial of MultiFlow are available at https://github.com/liuq-lab/MultiFlow.

records.title: Prediction transfer does not imply reliability transfer in single-cell foundation models.
records.abstract: Single-cell foundation models are increasingly transferred across tissues, diseases, perturbation screens, and experimental platforms. Although substantial effort has focused on prediction transfer, it remains unclear whether a model's assessment of its own reliability transfers similarly across biological contexts. Here we define reliability transfer as the ability to transfer an accurate assessment of when model predictions are likely to be correct or incorrect and investigate its behavior across ten perturbation-prediction systems spanning multiple datasets, models, and evaluation settings. We find that reliability transfer varies substantially across source-target pairs and cannot be inferred from predictive performance alone, indicating that prediction transfer and reliability transfer constitute distinct forms of generalization. Analyses of biological annotations, network connectivity, target exposure, and contextual factors reveal that prediction reliability is associated with both shared and context-dependent signals, with their relative importance differing across systems. To characterize this variability, we introduce reliability-attribution fingerprints, context-level signatures derived from strictly cross-fitted SHAP explanations that summarize how reliability estimators combine biological and contextual information when assigning confidence. Across systems, contexts with similar attribution-magnitude fingerprints tended to transfer reliability more successfully, and fingerprint similarity identified transfer sources achieving higher reliability-transfer performance within the observed candidate set. However, these relationships weakened under stricter cross-family transfer settings, indicating that transferable reliability structure remains partly dependent on shared contextual information. Finally, transferred reliability estimators produced different perturbation rankings despite identical perturbation predictions, illustrating a practical consequence of reliability transfer for downstream prioritization. Together, these results establish reliability transfer as a distinct aspect of foundation-model generalization and introduce reliability-attribution fingerprints as a framework for characterizing transferable reliability structure across biological contexts.

records.title: Artificial Cells and Biomimetic Cells: Intelligent Systems Driving a Paradigm Shift in Drug Discovery and Delivery.
records.abstract: The convergence of synthetic biology, materials science, and artificial intelligence drives a transformative shift in biopharmaceutical research, advancing from passive drug carriers to intelligent, programmable therapeutics. This review evaluates artificial and biomimetic cells as a framework that connects fundamental biological discovery with clinical translation. It examines five key technological pathways: membrane-engineered artificial cells, membraneless organelle (MLO) systems, multicompartmental artificial cells, protocell communication networks, and virtual cells. These platforms enable precise regulation of drug stability, targeting, biosynthesis, and adaptive responsiveness. Recent progress includes microenvironment-triggered release, logic-gated intercellular communication, and virtual cell-assisted high-throughput screening and toxicity prediction. Despite these advances, challenges remain in scalable manufacturing, long-term stability, and regulatory adaptation. The integration of closed-loop learning, interpretable models, and advanced biomanufacturing will be essential to position artificial and biomimetic cell systems at the forefront of next-generation precision medicine.

records.title: The Tenocyte from Atom to Cell: A Critical Multiscale Synthesis Linking Collagen Chemistry, Tissue Mechanics, Cell Mechanobiology and Mathematical Modelling.
records.abstract: The tenocyte builds, maintains, senses and degrades one of the most mechanically demanding extracellular matrices in vertebrates, yet the chemical, physical, biological and mathematical descriptions of this system have developed in largely separate literatures. This review examines the tenocyte-matrix unit as a single causal system spanning eight orders of magnitude in length, organised around five transitions: from collagen chemistry to molecular mechanics; from molecule to fibril and fascicle; from tissue loading to the cellular mechanical stimulus; from stimulus to transcription; and from cellular output back to matrix composition. At each transition, we weigh competing hypotheses, identify where evidence is decisive and where it remains correlative, and state the governing equations. We integrate advances from 2021-2026, including single-cell and spatial transcriptomic atlases of human tendons, the establishment of PIEZO1 as a causal regulator of tendon stiffness, and microstructurally derived constitutive models. We argue that tendon homeostasis is a closed-loop control problem, formalised as a mechanostat with an inverted-U dose-response, and that the recurrent pathologies of tendon-tendinopathy, ageing, diabetic stiffening and fibrotic healing are failures of this loop rather than of any single component. An open-source computational companion (tenocyte-virtual-cell) is introduced, and a prioritised research agenda closes the review.

records.title: Primary-Tumor Transcriptomic Signatures Associated with Circulating Tumor Cells Status in Breast Cancer: From CTC-Negative Remodeling to CTC-Associated Metastatic Programs.
records.abstract: Background/Objectives: Circulating tumor cells (CTCs) play a central role in metastasis by enabling tumor dissemination through the bloodstream. However, the molecular transition from CTC-negative (CTC-) to CTC-positive (CTC+) states and their associated systemic remodeling remain poorly understood. Methods: We performed a transcriptomic comparison between CTC+, CTC-, and healthy individuals using RNA-seq data and a bioinformatics pipeline. Differentially expressed genes (DEGs) were subjected to functional enrichment, protein-protein interaction (PPI) analysis, survival modeling, and drug perturbation prediction to delineate the molecular determinants of CTC emergence and persistence. Results: Primary tumors from CTC+ patients exhibited distinct transcriptomic profiles characterized by the upregulation of genes involved in PI3K-Akt signaling, extracellular matrix organization, and chromatin regulation (e.g., HDAC1, JUN, KLK10), alongside the downregulation of immune activation pathways, including complement, B-cell receptor (BCR), and T-cell receptor (TCR) signaling. Multi-gene survival models derived from upregulated (KLK10, MEOX2, IRS4, RND2) and downregulated (ALDH3A1, PPP2R2B, IGF1R) hub genes significantly stratified patient outcomes (HR = 1.74-2.44, p < 0.01). In contrast, primary tumors from CTC- patients displayed early systemic transcriptional alterations relative to healthy controls, with 1700+ DEGs linked to MAPK/ERK and receptor tyrosine kinase (RTK) signaling pathways, suggesting pre-metastatic immune reprogramming even before CTC detection. Drug repurposing analysis identified Trichostatin A, BX-795, and Alvocidib as candidate compounds capable of reversing the CTC+ transcriptional signature. Conclusions: Rather than supporting a strictly binary view of CTC status, our findings are consistent with a transcriptional continuum of distinct yet partially overlapping primary-tumor transcriptional states associated with CTC- and CTC+ status, highlighting a molecular shift from immune suppression to epigenetic adaptation that facilitates hematogenous dissemination. The identified multi-gene prognostic panels and small-molecule candidates provide a foundation for CTC-targeted therapeutic strategies and early detection biomarkers in breast cancer.

records.title: PFM: perturbed flow matching for structure-based drug design.
records.abstract: Target-specific 3D molecular generation is a promising approach for structure-based drug design. However, existing diffusion-based methods are generally restricted to marginal distributions with closed-form solutions, limiting the flexibility of generative process design, especially for the forward noising process. As a result, these methods may be less effective in modeling the complex distributions underlying pocket-conditioned molecular generation. We develop Perturbed Flow Matching (PFM), a flow-matching-based framework for protein pocket-conditioned 3D molecular generation. PFM employs a perturbed conditional probability path that incorporates both pocket binding-site information and coupled atom type-coordinate information, enabling more effective generation of molecules in protein binding environments. On CrossDocked2020, PFM achieves competitive structural quality and the best average Vina score among the evaluated unguided methods (-7.12); PFM-G further improves the score to -8.70 with tailored classifier-free guidance. Experiments on additional molecular datasets further confirm the effectiveness and generalizability of the proposed framework. https://github.com/kurisu92725/PFM.

records.title: De novo design of miniprotein inhibitors of bacterial adhesins.
records.abstract: The rise of multidrug-resistant bacterial infections necessitates the discovery of novel antimicrobial strategies. Here, we show that protein design provides a generalizable means of generating new antimicrobials by neutralizing the function of bacterial adhesins, which are virulence factors critical in host-pathogen interactions. We de novo designed high-affinity miniprotein binders to FimH and Abp chaperone usher pili adhesins from uropathogenic Escherichia coli and Acinetobacter baumannii, respectively, which are implicated in mediating both uncomplicated and catheter-associated urinary tract infections (UTI) responsible for significant morbidity worldwide. The designed antagonists have high specificity and stability, disrupt bacterial recognition of host receptors, block biofilm formation, and are effective in treating and preventing murine models of uncomplicated and catheter-associated UTIs in vivo.

records.title: Pharmacophore-Conditioned Diffusion Model for Ligand-Based De Novo Drug Design.
records.abstract: Developing bioactive molecules remains a central, time- and cost-heavy challenge in drug discovery, particularly for novel targets lacking structural or functional data. Pharmacophore modeling presents an alternative for capturing the key features required for molecular bioactivity against a biological target. In this work, we present PharmaDiff, a pharmacophore-conditioned diffusion model for 3D molecular generation. PharmaDiff employs a transformer-based architecture to integrate an atom-based representation of the 3D pharmacophore into the generative process, enabling the precise generation of 3D molecular graphs that align with predefined pharmacophore hypotheses. Through comprehensive testing, PharmaDiff demonstrates superior performance in matching 3D pharmacophore constraints compared to ligand-based drug design methods. Additionally, it achieves higher docking scores across a range of proteins in structure-based drug design, without the need for target protein structures. By integrating pharmacophore modeling with 3D generative techniques, PharmaDiff offers a powerful and flexible framework for rational drug design.

records.title: Programming Targeted Immune Cell Migration Using Orthogonal Chemokine-Receptor Pairs.
records.abstract: Chemokines orchestrate the migration of immune cells throughout the body, but harnessing chemokine signaling to engineer targeted cell trafficking is challenging because of their overlapping interactions and broad expression patterns. Here we used structure-guided protein design to engineer orthogonal chemokine-receptor pairs with minimal crosstalk to native systems. T cells engineered with an ortho-receptor selectively infiltrated tissues producing the ortho-chemokine, in vitro and in vivo. By engineering T cells that both sense and secrete the ortho-chemokine, we generated collective swarming behavior in which pioneer cells attract follower cells via an ortho-chemokine gradient self-organized by positive feedback. By providing orthogonal genetic control over both the generation and sensing of chemokine gradients, this system enables the construction of autonomous spatial targeting programs in engineered cells.

records.title: Reliable and Efficient Agentic Protein Design with Toolset Harnessing.
records.abstract: Computational protein design workflows require the orchestration of multiple tools, data formats, and analysis steps that are often fragmented. Here, we introduce Chaperone, a lightweight and customizable framework that enables seamless integration of RFdiffusion3 (RFD3) [1] with downstream sequence design, structure prediction, and evaluation tools, including ProteinMPNN [2], AlphaFold3 (AF3) [3], and more than 50 other protein design tools. By combining a programmable agent-friendly interface with parallelized execution on high-performance computing systems, Chaperone as a harness enables rapid iteration and scalable exploration of complex protein design workflows. Across an evaluation of nine biomolecular design tasks, we find using Chaperone reduces total token usage relative to baseline agents by 86% and GPU costs by 64%, while increasing the overall computational design pass rate. We demonstrate Chaperone's utility for large-scale design-space exploration through a two-week end-to-end small-molecule binder design campaign, yielding low nanomolar binders to cortisol zero shot. We further demonstrate its versatility across distinct design challenges, including the design of a symmetric 12-subunit self-assembly nanoparticle and a linker that mediates interactions between C2- and D3-symmetric protein complexes to form crystalline assemblies. Together, these results demonstrate how agent harnesses built around standardized tool interfaces can substantially improve the efficiency and success of complex, long-horizon agentic design workflows in biology. We make Chaperone freely available to the community on GitHub: https://github.com/RosettaCommons/chaperone .

records.title: MYC targeted de novo binders impair tumor growth.
records.abstract: MYC is one of the most frequently dysregulated oncogenic drivers across many cancers, yet direct therapeutic targeting has remained difficult because its function is mediated by disordered regions and transient protein-protein interactions. Here we design proteins that bind epitopes within regions of MYC whose sequence is conserved between human and mouse, including intrinsically disordered motifs required for oncogenic activity. In vitro, the designs bind MYC with nanomolar affinity and in cells they engage MYC, disrupt interactions with MAX, and remodel MYC-associated protein complexes. Expression of the binders decreases cell proliferation across diverse MYC-dependent hematopoietic, liver, pancreatic, and patient-derived tumor models, and in an orthotopic pancreatic cancer model, binder-expressing tumor cells were selectively depleted. This work establishes de novo protein design as a generalizable strategy to therapeutically target intrinsically disordered transcription factors. We developed a panel of de novo designed intracellular protein binders that target conserved functional regions of MYC with nanomolar affinity, remodel MYC complexes and interaction networks in cells, suppress proliferation across MYC-dependent cancer models, and are depleted from orthotopic pancreatic tumors in vivo.

records.title: Cellular Proliferation and Reprogramming in Pre-Metastatic Niches: Mechanisms and Therapeutic Vulnerabilities.
records.abstract: Cancer metastasis, the leading cause of cancer-related mortality, fundamentally depends on the proactive remodelling of distant organ microenvironments by primary tumours through systemic signals, creating a pre-metastatic niche before tumour cell arrival. This review systematically deconstructs the dynamic spatiotemporal evolution of the pre-metastatic niche, highlighting the multi-layered reprogramming of stromal, endothelial and immune cells that collectively cultivate a pro-tumourigenic and immunosuppressive microenvironment. We elucidate the biomechanical and biochemical sensing mechanisms, derived primarily from experimental models, that dictate the fate of disseminated tumour cells, governing the critical balance between dormancy maintenance and proliferative reactivation. Furthermore, we synthesize mechanistic insights alongside human tissue and liquid-biopsy correlative evidence on how metabolic resetting and epigenetic memory may contribute to sustaining pre-metastatic niche stability, and discuss how cutting-edge single-cell and spatial omics technologies are deciphering the intricate multicellular topological architecture of the niche. Ultimately, by mapping these complex systemic interactions across preclinical, biomarker and translational levels, we identify potential therapeutic vulnerabilities and advocate for a paradigm shift toward microenvironment normalization. While clinical validation remains an evolving frontier, targeting pre-metastatic niche priming represents a promising window that warrants rigorous clinical evaluation to intercept nascent metastasis before clinically detectable colonization occurs.

records.title: Clinical translation of liquid biopsy in early cancer screening: biofluid selection, model construction, and clinical validation.
records.abstract: Global cancer incidence continues to rise, underscoring the urgent need for effective early detection strategies. Liquid biopsy shows promise as a minimally invasive approach, yet only a limited number of assays have successfully transitioned from research to clinical practice. This review examines the critical decisions and challenges encountered along the translational pathway for liquid biopsy based early cancer screening, covering biofluid selection, biomarker characteristics, multi-omics integration, model construction, and the hierarchy of clinical evidence. We highlight the importance of biologically driven complementarity in biomarker combination, rigorous control group design, and prospective real-world validation, while also identifying key gaps that currently constrain clinical adoption. Collectively, these considerations aim to inform more efficient development strategies and help bridge the gap between technological innovation and clinically impactful tests.

records.title: Cerebrospinal fluid-derived small extracellular vesicles reveal a compartment-specific diagnostic signature for NSCLC leptomeningeal metastasis.
records.abstract: Leptomeningeal metastasis (LM) is a devastating complication of non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC), yet timely diagnosis remains challenging because conventional approaches, including magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) and cerebrospinal fluid (CSF) cytology, have limited sensitivity, particularly at initial presentation. Small extracellular vesicles (sEVs), as nanoscale carriers of protected regulatory cargo, have emerged as promising substrates for liquid biopsy. However, in anatomically compartmentalized central nervous system malignancies, the extent to which disease-associated sEV-miRNA signals are preserved across biofluids remains unclear. We profiled sEV-associated miRNAs by small RNA sequencing in CSF and plasma samples from NSCLC patients with clinically adjudicated LM status (NC, LM-, and LM+), including paired specimens where available. Biofluid-specific miRNA programs were characterized using weighted gene co-expression network analysis (WGCNA), and diagnostic models were developed using machine learning with Random Forest and LASSO-based feature selection. Model performance was evaluated in an independent validation cohort relative to final adjudicated LM status and compared with initial and cumulative MRI and CSF cytology assessments. CSF-derived sEV-associated miRNAs showed markedly stronger disease-stratification capacity than plasma-derived signals (ARI = 0.813 vs. 0.255; cluster purity = 0.868 vs. 0.694), revealing profound biofluid asymmetry. Network analysis identified a dominant LM-associated module in CSF (r = 0.74, P = 9 × 10⁻⁷) with limited preservation in plasma, indicating that LM-related vesicle-associated molecular programs are compartment-restricted. From this CSF-specific nanoscale vesicle signature, we derived a four-miRNA diagnostic panel comprising hsa-let-7e-5p, hsa-miR-30d-5p, hsa-miR-486-5p, and hsa-miR-375. In the independent validation cohort, the single-sample sEV-miRNA panel achieved an AUC of 0.935, with 86.4% sensitivity and 87.5% specificity. By comparison, initial MRI and initial CSF cytology showed sensitivities of 50.0% and 77.3%, respectively, whereas cumulative MRI and cumulative CSF cytology showed sensitivities of 70.0% and 86.4%, respectively. CSF-derived sEV-associated miRNAs encode an LM-proximal molecular program that is not faithfully captured in plasma, underscoring the importance of biofluid compartmentalization in nanobiotechnology-based biomarker discovery. Our findings establish a compartment-aware sEV-miRNA diagnostic strategy for accurate LM detection and provide a conceptual framework for extracellular vesicle-based molecular diagnostics in central nervous system malignancies.

records.title: Dual roles of ANXA7 in the early diagnosis and prognostic prediction of colorectal cancer: insights from serum exosome proteomics and single-cell transcriptomics.
records.abstract: Colorectal cancer (CRC) develops over 10-15 years from normal mucosa to advanced adenoma (AA) and invasive carcinoma; however, noninvasive biomarkers capable of detecting premalignant lesions and predicting the patient prognosis are still urgently needed. Circulating small extracellular vesicles (sEVs, exosomes) are nanoscale lipid bilayer carriers that are stably enriched in body fluids and serve as ideal liquid biopsy substrates for tumor molecular profiling. Nevertheless, most existing exosomal biomarker studies adopt binary case‒control designs, lack sequential adenoma‒carcinoma cohorts, and rarely combine exosomal proteomics with single-cell transcriptomics to trace the cellular origins of the biomarkers or construct paired diagnostic‒prognostic models. We integrated EXODUS rapid sEV isolation technology with 4D-DIA quantitative proteomics to profile serum exosomal proteomes across four sequential cohorts: healthy controls (NCs), patients with AA, patients with early CRC (ECRC), and patients with advanced CRC. Time series clustering and cross-cohort differential screening identified annexin A7 (ANXA7) as a continuously upregulated exosomal protein that accompanies malignant transformation in CRC. Western blotting and commercial ELISA verified the progressive increase in circulating sEV-ANXA7 levels, while tissue immunohistochemistry further confirmed the increase in ANXA7 expression from normal epithelium to adenoma and carcinoma epithelium. A single ROC curve analysis demonstrated that serum sEV-ANXA levels achieved an AUC of 0.821 for distinguishing healthy individuals from those with high-risk advanced adenomas. The combination of sEV-ANXA7 levels with the levels of the traditional markers CEA and CA199 significantly improved the diagnostic accuracy for both premalignant and early CRC lesions. Single-cell transcriptomic mining of public CRC datasets revealed a unique ANXA7⁺ epithelial progenitor cell (EPC) subpopulation, a distinct epithelial subset containing precancerous abnormal epithelial cells and early malignant epithelial cells with elevated malignant transformation potential, which was highly enriched in tumor tissues, which featured elevated stemness signatures, increased malignant scores, and the activation of ferroptosis and the P53 signaling pathway. The results of the CellChat analysis further revealed that ANXA7⁺ EPCs mediate tumor immune escape via CD8A-CEACAM5 ligand-receptor crosstalk with T cells. In vitro CCK-8 and EdU functional assays confirmed that ANXA7 markedly accelerated the proliferation of HCT116 and SW480 CRC cells. Based on the overlapping upregulated genes from ANXA7-high bulk tumors and ANXA7⁺ EPC subsets, we established a 12-gene LASSO prognostic signature, which exhibited robust performance in predicting 1-5-year survival (AUC > 0.68) of patients in both TCGA training cohort and the independent GEO validation cohort. Collectively, the results of this multiomics study reveal serum exosomal ANXA7 as a dual-function nanovesicle biomarker for early adenoma screening and the prognostic risk stratification of CRC and reveal the oncogenic ANXA7⁺ epithelial progenitor cell population that drives malignant colorectal progression. Our work provides translational evidence and theoretical basis for the development of exosome-based noninvasive liquid biopsy strategies and targeted therapeutic interventions against CRC.

records.title: Demonstrating the False-Positive Paradox in Radiology with Artificial Intelligence: Estimating Clinically Anticipated PPV, FDR, NPV, and FOR of FDA-Cleared Devices Using Performance Metrics from 510(k) Summaries and Prevalences from Local and Published Data.
records.abstract: The false-positive paradox (FPP) describes the counterintuitive phenomenon whereby a test can achieve high sensitivity and specificity yet still produce mostly false-positive results when applied to low-prevalence populations. This phenomenon is particularly relevant to radiology artificial intelligence (AI), where devices are typically marketed and cleared using diagnostic accuracy metrics such as sensitivity, specificity, and area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (ROC-AUC). However, these metrics do not indicate the proportion of false-positive and false-negative outputs clinicians should expect in local practice. This study estimated the positive predictive value (PPV), false discovery rate (FDR), negative predictive value (NPV), and false omission rate (FOR) for recent Food and Drug Administration (FDA)-cleared radiology AI devices by combining publicly reported 510(k) sensitivity and specificity with local or literature-derived prevalence estimates. Public FDA summaries for 38 radiology AI devices authorized in 2024 or 2025 were reviewed, yielding 57 target pathology entries. Median reported sensitivity, specificity, and ROC-AUC exceeded 90%; nevertheless, clinically anticipated FDRs were often high. For example, a large vessel occlusion detector with 90.6% sensitivity and 88.8% specificity was estimated to have a PPV of 29.3% and an FDR of 70.7% at a prevalence of 4.87%, meaning most positive AI alerts would be false positives. These findings do not evaluate device performance but instead illustrate the FPP in radiology AI. Public 510(k) summaries should consistently report sensitivity, specificity, and test set prevalence so that radiologists and other stakeholders can estimate PPV, FDR, NPV, and FOR for their own patient populations before implementation.
